title: American College of Sports Medicine position stand: Exercise and fluid replacement
claims: The goal of drinking during exercise is to prevent excessive dehydration, defined as more than 2% body weight loss from water deficit, and excessive changes in electrolyte balance.
There is considerable variability in sweating rates and sweat electrolyte content between individuals, so customised fluid replacement programmes are recommended.
Individual sweat rates can be estimated by measuring body weight before and after exercise.
During exercise, beverages containing electrolytes and carbohydrates can provide benefits over water alone under certain circumstances.
After exercise, the goal is to replace any fluid and electrolyte deficit; the speed of replacement depends on how quickly rehydration is needed and the size of the deficit.

claimVerification.note: 原文（During Exercise 一节）：“The goal of drinking during exercise is to prevent excessive dehydration (>2% BW loss from water deficit) and excessive changes in electrolyte balance to avert compromised exercise performance.”
原文：“There is considerable variability for water and electrolyte losses between individuals and between different activities”；“Individuals should develop customized fluid replacement programs…”

原文：“it is recommended that individuals should monitor body weight changes during training/competition sessions to estimate their sweat lost … This allows customized fluid replacement programs to be developed for each person's particular needs.”

原文：“Consumption of beverages containing electrolytes and carbohydrates can help sustain fluid-electrolyte balance and exercise performance”；同段说明“The need for these different components … will depend on the specific exercise task … and weather conditions”，与“under certain circumstances”相符。

原文：“After exercise, the goal is to fully replace any fluid and electrolyte deficit. The aggressiveness to be taken depends on the speed that rehydration must be accomplished and the magnitude of the fluid-electrolyte deficit.”
